description:
English Bluebell (Hyacinthoides non-scripta) is a spring bulb plant sometimes grown in gardens. It is unsafe for cats because the bulbs and above-ground parts can contain compounds that affect the stomach and heart.

The main concern is cardiac glycosides and related plant chemicals. These can irritate the digestive tract and, with enough exposure, disturb normal heart rhythm. The bulb is usually the highest-risk part because it stores more concentrated compounds.

A cat that eats English bluebell may vomit, have diarrhea, drool, seem weak, or act unusually tired. Higher exposures can be more serious. Keep bulbs and garden clippings away from cats, and call a veterinarian if your cat chews or eats any part of the plant.
